title.zh: 卷一百十九 周書10: 世宗本紀六
title.en: Volume 119 Book of Later Zhou 21: Shizong Annals 6
title.raw: 卷一百十九 周書10: 世宗本紀六 Volume 119 Book of Later Zhou 21: Shizong Annals 6

units.zh: 顯德六年春正月丁未朔，帝御崇元殿受朝賀，仗衛如式。
units.literal: In the sixth year of Xiansi, on dingwei the first day of the first month of spring, the Emperor took the throne in Chongyuan Hall to receive court congratulations; the guard of honor followed the prescribed formation.
units.idiomatic: On the first day of the first month of spring in the sixth year of Xiande, dingwei, the Emperor held audience in Chongyuan Hall to receive the New Year's felicitations, with the ceremonial guard arrayed according to regulation.

units.zh: 壬子，高麗國王王昭遣使貢方物。
units.literal: On renzi, King Wang Zhao of Goryeo sent envoys presenting local products.
units.idiomatic: On renzi, Wang Zhao, king of Goryeo, sent envoys bearing tribute goods.

units.zh: 己卯，以翰林學士、中書舍人申文炳為左散騎常侍。
units.literal: On jimao, Hanlin Academician and Secretariat Drafter Shen Wenbing was made Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.
units.idiomatic: On jimao, Shen Wenbing, Hanlin academician and secretariat drafter, was appointed Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.

units.zh: 晉州節度使楊廷璋奏，率兵入河東界，招降堡寨一十三所。
units.literal: Jin Prefecture Military Commissioner Yang Tingzhang memorialized that he had led troops into the Hedong frontier and induced thirteen fortified strongholds to surrender.
units.idiomatic: Yang Tingzhang of Jin reported that he had led troops into the Hedong frontier and induced thirteen fortified strongholds to surrender.

units.zh: 癸未，立魏王符彥卿女為皇后，仍令所司擇日備禮冊命。
units.literal: On guiwei, the daughter of Prince of Wei Fu Yanqing was installed as empress; the responsible offices were further ordered to choose a day and prepare the rites of investiture.
units.idiomatic: On guiwei, the daughter of Fu Yanqing, Prince of Wei, was installed as empress, and the responsible offices were ordered to choose a day for the investiture ceremony.

units.zh: 以皇長子宗訓為特進左衛上將軍，封梁王；
units.literal: The eldest imperial son Zongxun was made specially advanced General of the Left Guard and enfeoffed as Prince of Liang;
units.idiomatic: The eldest son Zongxun was made specially advanced general of the Left Guard and enfeoffed as Prince of Liang;

title.zh: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子
title.raw: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子 Volume 53 Biographies 23: Crown Prince Minhuai

units.zh: 愍懷太子
units.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai
units.idiomatic: Crown Prince Minhuai

units.zh: 湣懷太子遹，字熙祖，惠帝長子，母曰謝才人。
units.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.
units.idiomatic: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.

units.zh: 幼而聰慧，武帝愛之，恆在左右。
units.literal: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.
units.idiomatic: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.

units.zh: 初，賈后母郭槐欲以韓壽女為太子妃，太子亦欲婚韓氏以自固。
units.literal: Earlier Empress Jia's mother Guo Huai had wished to take Han Shou's daughter as crown princess; the crown prince also wished to marry the Hans to strengthen himself.
units.idiomatic: Earlier, Empress Jia's mother, Guo Huai, had wanted Han Shou's daughter to become crown princess. The crown prince also hoped that marrying into the Han family would strengthen his position.

units.zh: 而壽妻賈午及後皆不聽，而為太子聘王衍小女惠風。
units.literal: But Han Shou's wife Jia Wu and the empress both refused and instead betrothed the crown prince to Wang Yan's younger daughter Huifeng.
units.idiomatic: But Han Shou's wife Jia Wu and the empress both refused, and instead betrothed the crown prince to Wang Yan's younger daughter Huifeng.

units.zh: 太子聞衍長女美，而賈后為謐聘之，心不能平，頗以為言。
units.literal: The crown prince heard Wang's elder daughter was beautiful while the empress betrothed her to Jia Mi; his heart could not rest easy and he spoke of it often.
units.idiomatic: The crown prince heard Wang's elder daughter was beautiful while the empress betrothed her to Jia Mi; his heart could not rest easy and he spoke of it often.

title.zh: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子
title.raw: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子 Volume 53 Biographies 23: Crown Prince Minhuai

units.zh: 愍懷太子
units.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai
units.idiomatic: Crown Prince Minhuai

units.zh: 湣懷太子遹，字熙祖，惠帝長子，母曰謝才人。
units.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.
units.idiomatic: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.

units.zh: 幼而聰慧，武帝愛之，恆在左右。
units.literal: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.
units.idiomatic: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.

units.zh: 而于宮中為市，使人屠酤，手揣斤兩，輕重不差。
units.literal: Yet inside the palace he opened a market, had people butcher and sell ale, and weighed purchases in his own hands to the exact ounce.
units.idiomatic: Yet he set up a market inside the palace, had others butcher animals and sell wine, and judged weights with his own hands without error.

units.zh: 其母本屠家女也，故太子好之。
units.literal: His mother had been a butcher's daughter; therefore the crown prince delighted in it.
units.idiomatic: His mother was originally a butcher’s daughter, which is why the crown prince enjoyed this.

units.zh: 又令西園賣葵菜、藍子、雞、面之屬，而收其利。
units.literal: He also ordered the Western Garden to sell mallow, indigo seed, chickens, flour, and the like, pocketing the profit.
units.idiomatic: He also ordered the Western Garden to sell mallow, indigo seed, chickens, flour, and the like, pocketing the profit.

units.zh: 不了，吾當手了之。
units.literal: if she does not, I shall end her life with my own hands.
units.idiomatic: if she does not, I shall end her life with my own hands.

units.zh: 並謝妃共要克期而兩發，勿疑猶豫，致後患。
units.literal: Together with Consort Xie we agreed a joint date for simultaneous rising—do not hesitate and breed later trouble.
units.idiomatic: Together with Consort Xie we agreed a joint date for simultaneous rising—do not hesitate and breed later trouble.

units.zh: 茹毛飲血於三辰之下，皇天許當掃除患害，立道文為王，蔣為內主。
units.literal: We shall eat raw flesh and drink blood beneath the three luminaries; High Heaven grants us leave to sweep away the scourge, enthrone Daowen as king, and install Jiang as inner mistress.
units.idiomatic: We shall eat raw flesh and drink blood beneath the three luminaries; High Heaven grants us leave to sweep away the scourge, enthrone Daowen as king, and install Jiang as inner mistress.

units.zh: 是日太子游玄圃，聞有使者至，改服出崇賢門，再拜受詔，步出承華門，乘粗犢車。
units.literal: That day the crown prince roamed the Mystic Garden; hearing envoys arrived he changed clothes, exited Chongxian Gate, twice bowed receiving the edict, walked out Chenghua Gate, and rode a rough ox-cart.
units.idiomatic: That day the crown prince roamed the Mystic Garden; hearing envoys arrived he changed clothes, exited Chongxian Gate, twice bowed receiving the edict, walked out Chenghua Gate, and rode a rough ox-cart.

units.zh: 澹以兵仗送太子妃王氏、三皇孫于金墉城，考竟謝淑妃及太子保林蔣俊。
units.literal: Dan escorted Crown Princess Wang and the three imperial grandsons to Jinyong under armed guard, and interrogated Consort Xie and the crown prince’s Lady Baolin Jiang Jun to death.
units.idiomatic: Dan escorted Crown Princess Wang and the three imperial grandsons to Jinyong under armed guard, and interrogated Consort Xie and the crown prince’s Lady Baolin Jiang Jun to death.

units.zh: 明年正月，賈后又使黃門自首，欲與太子為逆。
units.literal: The next first month Empress Jia again had a Yellow Gate confess plotting rebellion with the crown prince.
units.idiomatic: The next first month Empress Jia again had a Yellow Gate confess plotting rebellion with the crown prince.

units.zh: 雖非中宮所生，奉事有如親母。
units.literal: Though not born of the inner palace I served her as my own mother.
units.idiomatic: Though not born of the inner palace I served her as my own mother.

units.zh: 自為太子以來，敕見禁檢，不得見母。
units.literal: Since becoming crown prince edicts confined me—I could not see my mother.
units.idiomatic: Since becoming crown prince, edicts confined me—I could not see my mother.

units.zh: 自宜城君亡，不見存恤，恆在空室中坐。
units.literal: Since the Lady of Yicheng died I received no comforting word—I constantly sat alone in empty rooms.
units.idiomatic: Since the Lady of Yicheng died I received no comforting word—I constantly sat alone in empty rooms.

title.zh: 卷63 王肅 宋弁
title.raw: 卷63 王肅 宋弁 Volume 63: Wang Su, Song Bian

units.zh: 王肅 宋弁
units.literal: Wang Su; Song Bian
units.idiomatic: Wang Su; Song Bian

units.zh: 王肅，字恭懿，琅邪臨沂人，司馬衍丞相導之後也。
units.literal: Wang Su, styled Gongyi, was a man of Linyi in Langye, a descendant of Chancellor Dao under Emperor Xiaowu (Sima Yan).
units.idiomatic: Wang Su, whose courtesy name was Gongyi, came from Linyi in Langye and was a descendant of Chancellor Wang Dao, who had served under Emperor Xiaowu (Sima Yan).

units.zh: 父奐，蕭賾尚書左僕射。
units.literal: His father Huan was Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat under Xiao Ze.
units.idiomatic: His father Wang Huan had served Xiao Ze as Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

units.zh: 武定末，著作佐郎。
units.literal: At the end of Wuding, Assistant Gentleman of the Academy.
units.idiomatic: At the end of the Wuding reign he served as Assistant Gentleman of the Academy.

units.zh: 紹，肅前妻謝生也，肅臨薨，謝始攜二女及紹至壽春。
units.literal: Shao was the son of Su's former wife, Lady Xie; when Su was near death, Xie at last brought her two daughters and Shao to Shouchun.
units.idiomatic: Shao was the son of Su's former wife, Lady Xie. When Su was dying, Lady Xie at last brought her two daughters and Shao to Shouchun.

units.zh: 世宗納其女為夫人，肅宗又納紹女為嬪。
units.literal: The Emperor Shizong took his daughter as Lady; the Emperor Suzong also took Shao's daughter as Imperial Concubine.
units.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong took his daughter as a consort, and Emperor Suzong later took Shao's daughter as an imperial concubine.

units.zh: 孔希學
units.literal: Kong Xixue
units.idiomatic: Kong Xixue

units.zh: 孔彥繩
units.literal: Kong Yanchang
units.idiomatic: Kong Yanchang

units.zh: 顏希惠曾質粹孔聞禮孟希文仲於陛周冕程接道程克仁張文運邵繼祖朱梴朱墅
units.literal: Yan Xihui, Zeng Zhicui, Kong Wenli, Meng Xiwen, Zhong Yubi, Zhou Mian, Cheng Jiedao, Cheng Keren, Zhang Wenyun, Shao Jizu, Zhu Ting, Zhu Shu
units.idiomatic: Yan Xihui, Zeng Zhicui, Kong Wenli, Meng Xiwen, Zhong Yubi, Zhou Mian, Cheng Jiedao, Cheng Keren, Zhang Wenyun, Shao Jizu, Zhu Ting, and Zhu Shu

units.zh: 卒，十六年，蔭鈺襲。
units.literal: He died; in the sixteenth year Yinyu inherited.
units.idiomatic: He died; Yinyu succeeded in the sixteenth year.

units.zh: 孟希文，字士煥，亞聖五十六代孫也。
units.literal: Meng Xiwen, courtesy name Shihuan, was a descendant of the Second Sage in the fifty-sixth generation.
units.idiomatic: Meng Xiwen, styled Shihuan, was a fifty-sixth-generation descendant of Mencius, the Second Sage.

units.zh: 洪武元年詔以孟子五十四代孫思諒奉祀，世復其家。
units.literal: In the first year of Hongwu an edict ordered Siliao, fifty-fourth-generation descendant of Mencius, to perform sacrifices, and his household was restored by hereditary grant.
units.idiomatic: In Hongwu 1 an edict appointed Siliao, fifty-fourth in descent from Mencius, to perform sacrifices and restored his household by hereditary grant.

units.zh: 卒，子元，字長伯，弘治二年襲。
units.literal: He died; his son Yuan, courtesy name Changbo, inherited in the second year of Hongzhi.
units.idiomatic: He died; his son Yuan, styled Changbo, succeeded in Hongzhi 2.

units.zh: 卒，子公棨幼，嘉靖二年以元弟亨之子公肇襲。
units.literal: He died; his son Gongqi was young; in the second year of Jiajing Yuan's younger brother Heng's son Gongzhao inherited.
units.idiomatic: He died leaving a young son Gongqi; in Jiajing 2 Yuan's nephew Gongzhao, son of his brother Heng, succeeded.

units.zh: 公肇，字先文，少好學，事繼母孔氏，以孝聞。
units.literal: Gongzhao, courtesy name Xianwen, loved study from youth and served his stepmother of the Kong clan with filial conduct, for which he was renowned.
units.idiomatic: Gongzhao, styled Xianwen, was studious from youth and famed for filial service to his Kong-clan stepmother.

units.idiomatic: Crown Prince Minhuai

units.zh: 湣懷太子遹，字熙祖，惠帝長子，母曰謝才人。
units.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.
units.idiomatic: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.

units.zh: 幼而聰慧，武帝愛之，恆在左右。
units.literal: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.
units.idiomatic: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.

units.zh: 時望氣者言廣陵有天子氣，故封為廣陵王，邑五萬戶。
units.literal: At the time, observers of celestial portents said Guangling had the aura of a Son of Heaven; therefore he was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangling with a fief of fifty thousand households.
units.idiomatic: Astrologers said Guangling bore an emperor's aura, so Yu was made Prince of Guangling with fifty thousand households.

units.zh: 以劉寔為師，孟珩為友，楊准、馮蓀為文學。
units.literal: Liu Shi was made tutor, Meng Heng companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun literary aides.
units.idiomatic: Liu Shi served as tutor, Meng Heng as companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun as literary aides.

units.zh: 惠帝即位，立為皇太子。
units.literal: When Emperor Hui succeeded to the throne, he was established as crown prince.
units.idiomatic: When Hui Di took the throne, Yu was made crown prince.

units.zh: 六月己卯，葬于顯平陵。
units.literal: On jimao day of the sixth month he was buried at Xianping Mausoleum.
units.idiomatic: On jimao day of the sixth month he was buried at Xianping Mausoleum.

units.zh: 帝感閻纘之言，立思子台，故臣江統、陸機並作誄頌焉。
units.literal: Moved by Yan Zuan's words the emperor raised a Terrace of Longing for Sons; former ministers Jiang Tong and Lu Ji both composed dirges.
units.idiomatic: Moved by Yan Zuan's words the emperor raised a Terrace of Longing for Sons; former ministers Jiang Tong and Lu Ji both composed dirges.

units.zh: 太子三子：虨、臧、尚，並與父同幽金墉。
units.literal: The crown prince had three sons—Bin, Zang, and Shang—all imprisoned with their father at Jinyong.
units.idiomatic: The crown prince had three sons—Bin, Zang, and Shang—all imprisoned with their father at Jinyong.

units.zh: 于洛侯 胡泥 李洪之 子神 張赦提 趙霸 崔暹 邸珍 田式 燕榮 元弘嗣 王文同
units.literal: Yu Luohou, Hu Ni, Li Hongzhi, Zi Shen, Zhang Sheti, Zhao Ba, Cui Xuan, Di Zhen, Tian Shi, Yan Rong, Yuan Hongsi, Wang Wentong
units.idiomatic: Yu Luohou, Hu Ni, Li Hongzhi, Zi Shen, Zhang Sheti, Zhao Ba, Cui Xuan, Di Zhen, Tian Shi, Yan Rong, Yuan Hongsi, and Wang Wentong

units.zh: 夫為國之體有四焉：一曰仁義，二曰禮制，三曰法令，四曰刑罰。
units.literal: The structure of governing a state has four elements: first, humanity and righteousness; second, ritual institutions; third, laws and decrees; fourth, punishments and penalties.
units.idiomatic: The foundation of statecraft rests on four pillars: humanity and righteousness, ritual institutions, laws and decrees, and punishments.

units.zh: 仁義、禮制，教之本也；
units.literal: Humanity, righteousness, and ritual institutions are the root of instruction;
units.idiomatic: Humanity, righteousness, and ritual are the roots of civilizing instruction;

units.zh: 未幾，榮死於蛆出之處。
units.literal: Before long Rong died at the place where the maggots had emerged.
units.idiomatic: Before long Rong died in that very place.

units.zh: 有子詢。
units.literal: He had a son Xun.
units.idiomatic: He had a son named Xun.

units.zh: 元弘嗣
units.literal: Yuan Hongsi
units.idiomatic: Yuan Hongsi

units.literal: Yang Zuo, style name Gongyi, originally a descendant of the Jinggong branch of the Yang clan of Tang; by Zuo's time the family had settled in Xuan.
units.idiomatic: Yang Zuo, courtesy name Gongyi, was descended from the Jinggong line of the Tang Yang clan; by his generation the family had made its home in Xuan.

units.zh: 及進士第，為陵州推官。
units.literal: When he attained the jinshi degree, he became judicial assistant in Ling Prefecture.
units.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, he served as judicial assistant in Ling Prefecture.

units.zh: 州有鹽井深五十丈，皆石也，底用柏木為幹，上出井口，垂綆而下，方能及水。
units.literal: The prefecture had a salt well fifty zhang deep, all stone; at the bottom cypress was used as a shaft lining, extending above the mouth of the well, with ropes let down before one could reach the water.
units.idiomatic: The prefecture had a salt well fifty zhang deep, cut entirely through rock. At the bottom a cypress-wood lining formed the shaft, rising above the mouth; only by lowering ropes could workers reach the water.

units.zh: 瑾素有操尚，所蒞以能稱，然御下苛嚴，少縱舍，好面折人短，以故多致訾怨。
units.literal: Jin had integrity throughout; wherever he served he was known for competence, yet he governed subordinates harshly with little leniency, liked to confront people's faults to their faces, and for this drew much criticism and resentment.
units.idiomatic: Jin had always been a man of principle and was regarded as capable wherever he served, yet he ruled subordinates with harsh severity and little mercy, and liked to expose others' faults to their faces — for which he earned much resentment.

units.zh: 閻詢，字議道，鳳翔天興人。
units.literal: Yan Xun, style name Yidao, was a native of Tianxing in Fengxiang.
units.idiomatic: Yan Xun, courtesy name Yidao, was a native of Tianxing in Fengxiang.

units.zh: 少時以學問著聞，擢進士第，又中書判拔萃科。
units.literal: Renowned for learning from youth, he passed the jinshi examination and also passed the Zhongshu exceptional-talent examination.
units.idiomatic: Known from youth for his scholarship, he passed the jinshi examination and also won the Zhongshu exceptional-talent selection.

units.zh: 兌居官論諫，無所表襮，先克承之。
units.literal: Dui, in office, remonstrated and counseled without displaying himself; earlier men had inherited this quality.
units.idiomatic: Dui counseled and remonstrated in office without parading his virtue; earlier generations had already embodied that same restraint.

units.zh: 掞之孝，燾之智，瑾之苛嚴，詢之辭令，皆著一時，自致顯官。
units.literal: Shan's filial piety, Dao's wisdom, Jin's harsh severity, and Xun's eloquence all stood out in their time, and each rose by his own efforts to high office.
units.idiomatic: Shan's filial devotion, Dao's shrewdness, Jin's harsh severity, and Xun's eloquence each made its mark in the age, and each won high office through his own merits.

units.zh: 俞充制軍禁暴，足為能臣，而希時相之意，倡請西征，使其不死，邊陲之禍，其可既乎？
units.literal: Yu Chong controlled the army and forbade violence—enough to count as a capable minister—yet he courted the chief minister's favor and advocated a western campaign. Had he not died, could the border calamities have ever ended?
units.idiomatic: Yu Chong kept the army in order and checked violence—he might well have been counted a capable minister—yet he curried favor with the chief minister and urged a western expedition. Had he lived, would the disasters on the frontier ever have ceased?

units.zh: 愍懷太子
units.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai
units.idiomatic: Crown Prince Minhuai

units.zh: 湣懷太子遹，字熙祖，惠帝長子，母曰謝才人。
units.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.
units.idiomatic: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.

units.zh: 幼而聰慧，武帝愛之，恆在左右。
units.literal: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.
units.idiomatic: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.

units.zh: 洗馬江統陳五事以諫之，太子不納，語在《統傳》中。
units.literal: Groom of the Household Jiang Tong presented five admonitions; the crown prince rejected them—the account appears in Jiang Tong's biography.
units.idiomatic: Groom of the Household Jiang Tong presented five admonitions; the crown prince rejected them—the account appears in Jiang Tong's biography.

units.zh: 舍人杜錫以太子非賈后所生，而後性凶暴，深以為憂，每盡忠規勸太子修德進善，遠於讒謗。
units.literal: Gentleman-of-the-Household Du Xi, because the crown prince was not Empress Jia's son and the empress was savage by nature, deeply worried; he repeatedly urged the crown prince to cultivate virtue and do good, standing far from slander.
units.idiomatic: Gentleman-of-the-Household Du Xi, because the crown prince was not Empress Jia's son and the empress was savage by nature, deeply worried; he repeatedly urged the crown prince to cultivate virtue and do good, standing far from slander.

units.zh: 太子怒，使人以針著錫常所坐氈中而剌之。
units.literal: The crown prince grew angry and had someone sew needles into Du Xi's usual felt mat to stab him.
units.idiomatic: Angered, Yu had someone put needles into the felt mat where Du Xi usually sat, so that they would prick him.

units.zh: 太子性剛，知賈謐恃後之貴，不能假借之。
units.literal: The crown prince's temper was stiff; knowing Jia Mi relied on the empress's power, he would not indulge him.
units.idiomatic: The crown prince's temper was stiff; knowing Jia Mi relied on the empress's power, he would not indulge him.

title.zh: 卷83 晉紀五
title.raw: 卷83 晉紀五

units.zh: 資治通鑑第083卷
units.literal: Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Government, Volume 83
units.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 83

units.zh: 【晉紀五】起屠維協洽，盡目章涒灘，凡二年。
units.literal: [Jin Records 5] beginning at gengwu, ending at guisi, altogether two years.
units.idiomatic: [Jin Records 5] runs from the year gengwu through guisi, spanning two years in all.

units.zh: 孝惠皇帝上之下元康九年（
units.literal: The lower portion of the first reign of Emperor Xiaohui, ninth year of Yuankang (
units.idiomatic: Under Emperor Hui of Jin, Yuankang, year 9 (

units.zh: 太子皆不從。
units.literal: The Heir Apparent would not follow any of them.
units.idiomatic: The heir apparent ignored every point.

units.zh: 中舍人杜錫，恐太子不得安其位，每盡忠諫，勸太子修德業，保令名，言辭懇切。
units.literal: Du Xi, Attendant of the Palace Secretariat, fearing the Heir Apparent could not secure his position, each time offered loyal remonstrance, urging the Heir Apparent to cultivate virtue and preserve his fine name, his words earnest.
units.idiomatic: Du Xi, Attendant of the Palace Secretariat, fearing the heir apparent might lose his position, repeatedly urged him in loyal remonstrance to cultivate virtue and preserve his good name, his words earnest and forceful.

units.zh: 太子患之，置針著錫常所坐氈中，刺之流血，錫，預之子也。
units.literal: The Heir Apparent resented this, placed needles in the mat where Xi usually sat, and pricked him until he bled. Xi was the son of Du Yu.
units.idiomatic: The heir apparent resented this, hid needles in the mat where Xi usually sat, and pricked him until he bled. Xi was the son of Du Yu.

units.zh: 太子性剛，知賈謐恃中宮驕貴，不能假借之。
units.literal: The Heir Apparent was by nature stern; knowing that Jia Mi relied on the central palace's arrogant eminence, he could not show him favor.
units.idiomatic: The heir apparent was proud by nature. Knowing Jia Mi relied on the empress's power, he would not indulge him.

title.zh: 卷46 列傳第38 孝義
title.raw: 卷46 列傳第38 孝義 Volume 46 Biographies 38: Filial Piety

units.zh: 李棠 柳檜 杜叔毗 荊可 秦族 皇甫遐 張元
units.literal: Li Tang, Liu Gui, Du Shubi, Jing Ke, Qin Zu, Huangfu Xia, Zhang Yuan
units.idiomatic: Li Tang, Liu Gui, Du Shubi, Jing Ke, Qin Zu, Huangfu Xia, and Zhang Yuan

units.zh: 夫塞天地而橫四海者，其唯孝乎；
units.literal: As for what fills Heaven and Earth and spans the four seas—is it not filial piety alone?
units.idiomatic: What fills Heaven and Earth and spans the four seas—is it not filial piety alone?

units.zh: 奉大功而立顯名者，其唯義乎。
units.literal: As for what upholds great merit and establishes illustrious fame—is it not righteousness alone?
units.idiomatic: What sustains great merit and wins illustrious fame—is it not righteousness alone?

units.zh: 使未反，而循中直兵參軍曹策、參軍劉曉謀以城降武。
units.literal: The envoy had not yet returned when Xun's Direct Troops Attendant Cao Ce and Attendant Liu Xiao plotted to surrender the city to Wu.
units.idiomatic: The envoy had not yet returned when Xun's Direct Troops Attendant Cao Ce and Attendant Liu Xiao plotted to surrender the city to Wu.

units.zh: 時叔毗兄君錫為循中記室參軍，從子映錄事參軍，映弟晰中直兵參軍，竝有文武材畧，各領部曲數百人。
units.literal: At the time Shubi's elder brother Junxi was Recorder in Xun's headquarters, his nephew Ying was Recording Attendant, and Ying's younger brother Xi was Direct Troops Attendant—all had civil and military talent and strategy, each leading several hundred men in their retinues.
units.idiomatic: At the time Shubi's elder brother Junxi was Recorder in Xun's headquarters, his nephew Ying was Recording Attendant, and Ying's younger brother Xi was Direct Troops Attendant—all had civil and military talent, each leading several hundred men in their retinues.

units.zh: 策等忌之，懼不同己，遂誣以謀叛，擅加害焉。
units.literal: Ce and the rest envied them, fearing they would not agree with themselves, and therefore falsely accused them of plotting rebellion and on their own authority harmed them.
units.idiomatic: Ce and the rest envied them, fearing they would not join them, and therefore falsely accused them of plotting rebellion and killed them on their own authority.

units.zh: 循尋討策等，擒之，斬曉而免策。
units.literal: Xun soon investigated Ce and the rest, seized them, executed Xiao and spared Ce.
units.idiomatic: Xun soon investigated Ce and the rest, seized them, executed Xiao and spared Ce.

title.raw: 卷九十三 列傳第六十三 外戚 Volume 93 Biographies 63: Imperial Affines

units.zh: 詳觀往誥，逖聽前聞，階緣外戚以致顯榮者，其所由來尚矣。
units.literal: Carefully examining the admonitions of old and heeding what was heard in former times, those who climbed by ties to imperial affines to reach high honor—their origins go back a long way.
units.idiomatic: A close reading of past injunctions and the lessons of earlier ages shows that riding kinship with the imperial consorts to wealth and rank is an old story.

units.zh: 而多至禍敗，鮮克令終者，何哉？
units.literal: Yet many come to disaster and ruin, and few achieve a good end—why?
units.idiomatic: Yet so many of them end in ruin, and precious few die in peace. Why is that?

units.zh: 豈不由祿以恩升，位非德舉；
units.literal: Is it not because emolument rises through favor, and office is not raised up by virtue?
units.idiomatic: Surely it is because their salaries come from imperial favor rather than merit, and their posts are not won by moral weight.

units.zh: 亮在列傳。
units.literal: Liang is in the arrayed biographies.
units.idiomatic: Yu Liang has his own biography elsewhere.

units.zh: 杜乂，字弘理，成恭皇后父，鎮南將軍預孫，尚書左丞錫之子也。
units.literal: Du Yi, styled Hongli, was the father of Empress Chenggong, grandson of South-Pacifying General Yu, and son of Left Assistant Director Xi.
units.idiomatic: Du Yi, courtesy name Hongli, father of Empress Chenggong, was a grandson of Du Yu, South-Pacifying General, and son of Du Xi, Left Assistant Director in the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 性純和，美姿容，有盛名于江左。
units.literal: By nature pure and mild, handsome in bearing, he had a great reputation south of the Yangzi.
units.idiomatic: Gentle in temper and strikingly handsome, he was famous throughout the south.

units.zh: 劉毅
units.literal: Liu Yi.
units.idiomatic: Liu Yi.

units.zh: 劉毅，字仲雄，東萊掖人。
units.literal: Liu Yi, courtesy name Zhongxiong, was a native of Ye in Donglai commandery.
units.idiomatic: Liu Yi, styled Zhongxiong, came from Ye in Donglai.

units.zh: 漢城陽景王章之後。
units.literal: He was descended from Prince Jing of Chengyang, Liu Zhang, of the Han.
units.idiomatic: He traced his ancestry to Prince Jing of Chengyang, Liu Zhang, under the Han.

units.zh: 語在《后傳》。
units.literal: Language is in Empress's biography.
units.idiomatic: (See the "Biography of Empress Yang.")

units.zh: 顒見表，大怒，遣陳顏、呂朗率騎五千收暾，暾東奔高密王略。
units.literal: Yong seeing the memorial raged—sent Chen Yan and Lu Lang with five thousand riders to seize Tun—Tun fled east to Prince of Gaomi Lue.
units.idiomatic: Yong sent riders to arrest Tun—who fled to Prince Lue.

units.zh: 會劉根作逆，略以暾為大都督，加鎮軍將軍討根。
units.literal: When Liu Gen rebelled—Lue made Tun grand commander—added general Who Guards the Army to strike Gen.
units.idiomatic: During Liu Gen's revolt Lue named Tun commander-in-chief to crush him.

units.zh: 暾戰失利，還洛。
units.literal: Tun fought—lost—returned Luoyang.
units.idiomatic: He lost and fell back to Luoyang.

units.zh: 愍懷太子
units.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai
units.idiomatic: Crown Prince Minhuai

units.zh: 湣懷太子遹，字熙祖，惠帝長子，母曰謝才人。
units.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.
units.idiomatic: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.

units.zh: 幼而聰慧，武帝愛之，恆在左右。
units.literal: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.
units.idiomatic: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.

units.zh: 其遊處左右，宜得正人使共周旋，能相長益者。」
units.literal: Those who attend him in leisure and service should be upright men who may keep company with him and mutually aid one another's growth."
units.idiomatic: Those about him in leisure and attendance should be upright men who keep company with him and help one another improve."

units.zh: 於是使太保衛瓘息庭、司空泰息略、太子太傅楊濟息毖、太子少師裴楷息憲、太子少傅張華息禕、尚書令華暠息恆與太子游處，以相輔導焉。
units.literal: Thereupon Grand Guardian Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Grand Mentor to the Crown Prince Yang Ji's son Bi, Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince Pei Kai's son Xian, Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Minister Director Hua Gao's son Heng were assigned to keep company with the crown prince and assist in his guidance.
units.idiomatic: Thereupon Grand Guardian Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Grand Mentor to the Crown Prince Yang Ji's son Bi, Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince Pei Kai's son Xian, Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Minister Director Hua Gao's son Heng were assigned to keep company with the crown prince and assist in his guidance.

units.zh: 及長，不好學，惟與左右嬉戲，不能尊敬保傅。
units.literal: When grown he cared nothing for study and only played games with attendants; he could not honor tutors or guardians.
units.idiomatic: When grown he cared nothing for study and only played games with attendants; he could not honor tutors or guardians.

title.zh: 卷三十七 列傳第七 宗室
title.raw: 卷三十七 列傳第七 宗室 Volume 37 Biographies 7: Imperial Clan

units.zh: 安平獻王孚
units.literal: Prince Fu of Anping with posthumous title Xian (section heading).
units.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Anping, Sima Fu.

units.zh: 安平獻王孚，字叔達，宣帝次弟也。
units.literal: Prince Xian of Anping, Sima Fu, courtesy name Shuda, was Emperor Xuan's next younger brother.
units.idiomatic: Sima Fu, Prince Xian of Anping, styled Shuda, was the younger brother who followed Emperor Xuan (Sima Yi).

units.zh: 初，孚長兄朗字伯達，宣帝字仲達，孚弟馗字季達，恂字顯達，進字惠達，通字雅達，敏字幼達，俱知名，故時號為「八達」焉。
units.literal: At first Fu's eldest brother Lang had courtesy name Boda; Emperor Xuan had courtesy name Zhongda; Fu's younger brothers were Kui, courtesy Jida; Xun, Xianda; Jin, Huida; Tong, Yada; and Min, Youda; all were renowned, so people at the time called them the 'Eight Worthies.'
units.idiomatic: At first Fu's eldest brother Lang had courtesy name Boda; Emperor Xuan had courtesy name Zhongda; Fu's younger brothers were Kui, courtesy Jida; Xun, Xianda; Jin, Huida; Tong, Yada; and Min, Youda; all were renowned, so people at the time called them the 'Eight Worthies.'

units.zh: 子孝王略
units.literal: Son Prince Xiao Lue.
units.idiomatic: Prince Xiao Sima Lue.

units.zh: 孝王略，字元簡，孝敬慈順，小心下士，少有父風。
units.literal: Prince Xiao Lue courtesy Yuanjian was respectful, mild, and obedient, humble toward scholars, having somewhat his father's manner.
units.idiomatic: Sima Lue, styled Yuanjian, echoed his father's modest courtesy.

units.zh: 元康初，湣懷太子在東宮，選大臣子弟有名稱者以為賓友，略與華恆等並侍左右。
units.literal: Early Yuankang Crown Prince Minhuai was in the eastern palace and chose sons of eminent ministers with reputation as guests and friends; Lue together with Hua Heng and others attended left and right.
units.idiomatic: Yuankang saw Lue among Minhuai's cultivated companions with Hua Heng.

units.zh: 曆散騎黃門侍郎、散騎常侍、秘書監，出為安南將軍、持節、都督沔南諸軍事，遷安北將軍、都督青州諸軍事。
units.literal: He successively held irregular cavalry yellow-gate gentleman, irregular cavalry attendant, palace library supervisor; went out Pacifying South General credential-bearing supervising Hannan military affairs; promoted Pacifying North General supervising Qing province military affairs.
units.idiomatic: He successively served as Yellow-Gate Gentleman Attendant, Regular Palace Attendant, and Director of the Palace Library; then he was sent out as General Who Pacifies the South, Bearer of the Staff, and commander of the armies south of the Mian, before being promoted to General Who Pacifies the North and commander of Qing Province military affairs.

units.zh: 略逼青州刺史程牧，牧避之，略自領州。
units.literal: Lue pressured Qing Inspector Cheng Mu until Mu yielded and Lue personally headed the province.
units.idiomatic: He bullied Cheng Mu aside and seized Qingzhou himself.

units.zh: 永興初，㡉令劉根起兵東萊，誑惑百姓，眾以萬數，攻略於臨淄，略不能距，走保聊城。
units.literal: Early Yongxing Magistrate Liu Gen of Yi county raised troops in Donglai deluding commoners tens of thousands strong raiding Lue at Linzi; Lue could not resist and fled defending Liaocheng.
units.idiomatic: Yongxing opened with Liu Gen's Donglai rising that drove Lue from Linzi to Liaocheng.

units.zh: 懷帝即位，遷使持節、都督荊州諸軍事、征南大將軍、開府儀同三司。
units.literal: When Emperor Huai ascended Lue was promoted credential-bearing supervisor of Jing military affairs, southern expedition grand marshal with independent headquarters matching Three Lords.
units.idiomatic: Huai made him credential-bearing Jing commander with three-dukes parity staff.

units.zh: 京兆流人王逌與叟人郝洛聚眾數千，屯于冠軍。
units.literal: Wang You, a displaced person from Jingzhao, and Hao Luo of the Sou people gathered several thousand followers and encamped at Guanjun.
units.idiomatic: Wang You, a displaced person from Jingzhao, and Hao Luo of the Sou people gathered several thousand followers and encamped at Guanjun.

units.zh: 略遣參軍崔曠率將軍皮初、張洛等討逌，為逌所譎，戰敗。
units.literal: Lue sent his military adviser Cui Kuang to lead the generals Pi Chu, Zhang Luo, and others against You, but You deceived them and they were defeated in battle.
units.idiomatic: Lue sent his military adviser Cui Kuang to lead the generals Pi Chu, Zhang Luo, and others against You, but You deceived them and they were defeated in battle.

units.zh: 略更遣左司馬曹攄統曠等進逼逌。
units.literal: Lue then sent Left Sima Cao Shu to lead Kuang and the others in advancing against You.
units.idiomatic: Lue then sent Left Sima Cao Shu to lead Kuang and the others in advancing against You.

units.zh: 將大戰，曠在後密自退走，攄軍無繼，戰敗，死之。
units.literal: As they were about to fight a major battle, Kuang, who was in the rear, secretly withdrew; Shu's army was left without support, was defeated, and Shu died in the fighting.
units.idiomatic: As they were about to fight a major battle, Kuang, who was in the rear, secretly withdrew; Shu's army was left without support, was defeated, and Shu died in the fighting.

units.zh: 略乃赦曠罪，復遣部將韓松又督曠攻逌，逌降。
units.literal: Lue then pardoned Kuang's offense and again sent his subordinate general Han Song to command Kuang in attacking You; You surrendered.
units.idiomatic: Lue then pardoned Kuang's offense and again sent his subordinate Han Song to lead Kuang against Wang You, who surrendered.

units.zh: 尋進開府，加散騎常侍。
units.literal: Soon he was advanced and allowed to establish his own office, with the additional appointment of Regular Mounted Attendant.
units.idiomatic: Soon he was advanced and allowed to establish his own office, with the additional appointment of Regular Mounted Attendant.

units.zh: 永嘉三年薨，追贈侍中、太尉，子據立。
units.literal: In the third year of Yongjia, he died and was posthumously granted the offices of Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant; his son Ju succeeded him.
units.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Yongjia and was posthumously granted the offices of Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant; his son Ju succeeded him.

units.zh: 薨，無子，以彭城康王子紘為嗣。
units.literal: He died without sons; Prince Kang of Pengcheng's son Hong was appointed successor.
units.idiomatic: Childless, he passed to Hong from Pengcheng's Kang line.

units.zh: 其後紘歸本宗，立紘子俊以奉其祀。
units.literal: Later Hong returned to root lineage; Hong's son Jun was established to maintain his sacrifices.
units.idiomatic: Hong reverted to his birth house; Jun kept Lue's line alive.

units.zh: 略兄新蔡武哀王騰
units.literal: Lue's elder brother Prince Wuai of Xincai Teng.
units.idiomatic: Lue's elder brother Sima Teng, Prince Wuai of Xincai.

units.zh: 新蔡武哀王騰，字元邁，少拜冗從僕射，封東嬴公，曆南陽、魏郡太守，所在稱職，徵為宗正，遷太常，轉持節、寧北將軍、都督并州諸軍事、并州刺史。
units.literal: Prince Wuai of Xincai Teng courtesy Yuanmai in youth was appointed supernumerary chariot master and enfeoffed Duke of Dongying; successively governor of Nanyang and Wei commandery where he was praised competent; summoned Grand Director of the Imperial Clan; promoted Minister of Ceremonies; transferred credential-bearing Pacifying North General supervising Bing military affairs and Bing Inspector.
units.idiomatic: Sima Teng, Prince Wuai of Xincai, courtesy name Yuanmai, was appointed Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant when young and enfeoffed as Duke of Dongying. He served successively as governor of Nanyang and Wei Commandery, was praised as competent wherever he served, was summoned as Director of the Imperial Clan, promoted to Minister of Ceremonies, and then transferred as Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the North, commander of all military affairs in Bing Province, and inspector of Bing Province.

units.zh: 宋受禪，國除。
units.literal: When Song accepted the abdication the state was abolished.
units.idiomatic: Liu Song ended the fief.

units.zh: 略弟南陽王模
units.literal: Younger brother of Lue Mo Prince of Nanyang.
units.idiomatic: Sima Mo, Prince of Nanyang—Lue's brother.

units.zh: 南陽王模，字元表，少好學，與元帝及范陽王虓俱有稱於宗室。
units.literal: Prince of Nanyang Mo courtesy Yuanbiao in youth loved learning and together with Yuan Di and Prince Xiao of Fanyang was praised within the imperial clan.
units.idiomatic: Mo, styled Yuanbiao, studied hard alongside Sima Rui and Sima Xiao.

title.zh: 卷三十七 列傳第七 宗室
title.raw: 卷三十七 列傳第七 宗室 Volume 37 Biographies 7: Imperial Clan

units.zh: 安平獻王孚
units.literal: Prince Fu of Anping with posthumous title Xian (section heading).
units.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Anping, Sima Fu.

units.zh: 安平獻王孚，字叔達，宣帝次弟也。
units.literal: Prince Xian of Anping, Sima Fu, courtesy name Shuda, was Emperor Xuan's next younger brother.
units.idiomatic: Sima Fu, Prince Xian of Anping, styled Shuda, was the younger brother who followed Emperor Xuan (Sima Yi).

units.zh: 初，孚長兄朗字伯達，宣帝字仲達，孚弟馗字季達，恂字顯達，進字惠達，通字雅達，敏字幼達，俱知名，故時號為「八達」焉。
units.literal: At first Fu's eldest brother Lang had courtesy name Boda; Emperor Xuan had courtesy name Zhongda; Fu's younger brothers were Kui, courtesy Jida; Xun, Xianda; Jin, Huida; Tong, Yada; and Min, Youda; all were renowned, so people at the time called them the 'Eight Worthies.'
units.idiomatic: At first Fu's eldest brother Lang had courtesy name Boda; Emperor Xuan had courtesy name Zhongda; Fu's younger brothers were Kui, courtesy Jida; Xun, Xianda; Jin, Huida; Tong, Yada; and Min, Youda; all were renowned, so people at the time called them the 'Eight Worthies.'

units.zh: 紘子俊
units.literal: Hong's son Jun.
units.idiomatic: Hong's son Jun.

units.zh: 恭王俊字道度，出嗣高密王略，官至散騎常侍。
units.literal: Prince Gong Jun courtesy Daodu went out to succeed Prince of Gaomi Lue and reached irregular cavalry attendant.
units.idiomatic: Prince Gong Sima Jun, styled Daodu, continued Lue of Gaomi and rose to supernumerary cavalry attendant.

units.zh: 薨，子敬王純之立，曆臨川內史、司農少府卿、太宰右長史。
units.literal: He died; his son Chunzhi, Prince Jing, succeeded him and successively held the offices of administrator of Linchuan, minister of agriculture, minister of the privy treasury, and right chief clerk to the Grand Steward.
units.idiomatic: When he died, his son Chunzhi, Prince Jing, succeeded him. He successively served as administrator of Linchuan, minister of agriculture, minister of the privy treasury, and right chief clerk to the Grand Steward.

units.zh: 雖並不能振施，其餘莫得比焉。
units.literal: Though neither could relieve distress broadly none others matched them.
units.idiomatic: Neither dispensed charity widely yet none surpassed their discipline.

units.zh: 泰四子：越、騰、略、模。
units.literal: Tai had four sons: Yue, Teng, Lue, Mo.
units.idiomatic: Four sons: Yue, Teng, Lue, Mo.

units.zh: 越自有傳。
units.literal: Yue has his own biography.
units.idiomatic: Yue appears elsewhere.

units.zh: 騰出後叔父，弟略立。
units.literal: Teng went out to succeed uncle; younger brother Lue succeeded.
units.idiomatic: Teng was adopted out; Lue inherited.

units.zh: 子孝王略
units.literal: Son Prince Xiao Lue.
units.idiomatic: Prince Xiao Sima Lue.

units.zh: 孝王略，字元簡，孝敬慈順，小心下士，少有父風。
units.literal: Prince Xiao Lue courtesy Yuanjian was respectful, mild, and obedient, humble toward scholars, having somewhat his father's manner.
units.idiomatic: Sima Lue, styled Yuanjian, echoed his father's modest courtesy.

title.zh: 卷83 晉紀五
title.raw: 卷83 晉紀五

units.zh: 資治通鑑第083卷
units.literal: Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Government, Volume 83
units.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 83

units.zh: 【晉紀五】起屠維協洽，盡目章涒灘，凡二年。
units.literal: [Jin Records 5] beginning at gengwu, ending at guisi, altogether two years.
units.idiomatic: [Jin Records 5] runs from the year gengwu through guisi, spanning two years in all.

units.zh: 孝惠皇帝上之下元康九年（
units.literal: The lower portion of the first reign of Emperor Xiaohui, ninth year of Yuankang (
units.idiomatic: Under Emperor Hui of Jin, Yuankang, year 9 (

units.zh: 虨疾篤，太子為之禱祀求福。
units.literal: When Bin's illness grew grave, the Heir Apparent prayed and offered sacrifices to seek blessing for him.
units.idiomatic: As Bin grew gravely ill, the heir apparent prayed and offered sacrifices on his behalf.

units.zh: 賈后聞之，乃詐稱帝不豫，召太子入朝，既至，后不見，置於別室，遣婢陳舞以帝命賜太子酒三升，使盡飲之。
units.literal: When Empress Jia heard of it she falsely announced the emperor was unwell and summoned the Heir Apparent to court; once he arrived the empress did not see him but placed him in a separate room and sent the maid Chen Wu, in the emperor's name, to bestow three pints of wine on the Heir Apparent and order him to drink it all.
units.idiomatic: Empress Jia heard of this and falsely announced that the emperor was ill, summoning the heir apparent to court. When he arrived she refused to see him, placed him in a side room, and sent the maid Chen Wu with the emperor's name to give him three pints of wine and order him to drink it all.

units.zh: 太子辭以不能飲三升，舞逼之曰：「不孝邪！
units.literal: The Heir Apparent declined, saying he could not drink three pints; Wu pressed him: "Are you unfilial!
units.idiomatic: He declined, saying he could not drink so much. Wu pressed him: "Are you unfilial?

units.zh: 天賜汝酒而不飲，酒中有惡物邪！」
units.literal: Heaven bestows wine upon you and you will not drink—is there something evil in the wine!"
units.idiomatic: Heaven grants you wine and you refuse. Do you think it poisoned?"

title.zh: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子
title.raw: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子 Volume 53 Biographies 23: Crown Prince Minhuai

units.zh: 愍懷太子
units.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai
units.idiomatic: Crown Prince Minhuai

units.zh: 湣懷太子遹，字熙祖，惠帝長子，母曰謝才人。
units.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.
units.idiomatic: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.

units.zh: 幼而聰慧，武帝愛之，恆在左右。
units.literal: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.
units.idiomatic: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.

units.zh: 十二月，賈后將廢太子，詐稱上不和，呼太子入朝。
units.literal: In the twelfth month, when Empress Jia would depose the crown prince, she falsely claimed the emperor was unwell and summoned the crown prince to court.
units.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, when Empress Jia would depose the crown prince, she falsely claimed the emperor was unwell and summoned the crown prince to court.

units.zh: 既至，後不見，置於別室，遣婢陳舞賜以酒棗，逼飲醉之。
units.literal: When he arrived she did not receive him but lodged him in a side chamber, sent maid Chen Wu with ale and jujubes, and forced him drunk.
units.idiomatic: When he arrived she did not receive him but lodged him in a side chamber, sent maid Chen Wu with ale and jujubes, and forced him drunk.

units.zh: 使黃門侍郎潘岳作書草，若禱神之文，有如太子素意，因醉而書之，令小婢承福以紙筆及書草使太子書之。
units.literal: She had Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Pan Yue draft a prayer text mimicking the crown prince's usual intent; because he was drunk she made him copy it, having the young maid Chengfu bring paper, brush, and draft.
units.idiomatic: She had Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Pan Yue draft a prayer text mimicking the Crown Prince's usual intent; because he was drunk she made him copy it, having the young maid Chengfu bring paper, brush, and draft.

units.zh: 二十九日早入見國家，須臾遣至中宮。
units.literal: On the twenty-ninth morning I entered and saw His Majesty; presently I was sent to the inner palace.
units.idiomatic: On the twenty-ninth morning I entered and saw His Majesty; presently I was sent to the inner palace.

units.zh: 中宮左右陳舞見語：'中宮旦來吐不快。
units.literal: Chen Wu, an attendant of the empress, told me: 'The empress vomited this morning and is unwell.'
units.idiomatic: Inner attendants Chen Wu told me: 'The empress vomited ill this morning.'

units.zh: '使住空屋中坐。
units.literal: I was made to sit in an empty chamber.
units.idiomatic: She told me to wait seated in an empty chamber.

units.zh: 須臾中宮遣陳舞見語：'聞汝表陛下為道文乞王，不得王是成國耳。
units.literal: Presently the empress sent Chen Wu to tell me: 'I hear you petitioned His Majesty to make Daowen a prince and were refused. A princely title means a territorial domain, after all.'
units.idiomatic: Presently the empress sent Chen Wu to tell me: 'I hear you petitioned His Majesty to make Daowen a prince and were refused. A princely title means a territorial domain, after all.'

units.zh: '中宮遙呼陳舞：'昨天教與太子酒棗。
units.literal: The empress called to Chen Wu from a distance: "Yesterday His Majesty ordered wine and jujubes for the crown prince."
units.idiomatic: The empress called to Chen Wu from a distance: "Yesterday His Majesty ordered wine and jujubes for the crown prince."

units.zh: '便持三升酒、大盤棗來見與，使飲酒啖棗盡。
units.literal: She brought three sheng of ale and a great tray of jujubes and made me finish both.
units.idiomatic: She brought three sheng of ale and a great tray of jujubes and made me finish both.

units.zh: 鄙素不飲酒，即便遣舞啟說不堪三升之意。
units.literal: I never drink ale yet sent Chen Wu back explaining I could not manage three sheng.
units.idiomatic: I never drink ale, yet sent Chen Wu back explaining I could not manage three sheng.

units.zh: 中宮遙呼曰：'汝常陛下前持酒可喜，何以不飲？
units.literal: The empress called from a distance: 'You are always so pleasing when you hold wine before His Majesty; why will you not drink?'
units.idiomatic: The empress called from a distance: 'You are always so pleasing when you hold wine before His Majesty; why will you not drink?'

units.zh: 又未見殿下，飲此或至顛倒。
units.literal: Nor had I yet seen Your Highness—I feared drink might overturn me.
units.idiomatic: Besides, I had not yet seen Your Highness, and drinking this might leave me confused and unsteady.

units.zh: '陳舞復傳語云：'不孝那！
units.literal: Chen Wu relayed another message: "You unfilial wretch!
units.idiomatic: Chen Wu relayed another message: 'You unfilial wretch!

units.zh: 天與汝酒飲，不肯飲，中有惡物邪？
units.literal: His Majesty gives you wine to drink, yet you refuse. Is there something harmful in it?"
units.idiomatic: His Majesty gives you wine to drink, yet you refuse. Is there something harmful in it?'

title.zh: 卷十六 列傳第八 段榮 子韶
title.en: Volume 16 Biographies 8: Duan Rong; Duan Shao
title.raw: 卷十六 列傳第八 段榮 子韶 Volume 16 Biographies 8: Duan Rong; Duan Shao

units.zh: 段榮 子韶
units.literal: Duan Rong; Duan Shao
units.idiomatic: Duan Rong; Duan Shao

units.zh: 段榮，字子茂，姑臧武威人也。
units.literal: Duan Rong, styled Zimao, was a native of Guzang in Wuwei.
units.idiomatic: Duan Rong, styled Zimao, was a native of Guzang in Wuwei.

units.zh: 祖信，仕沮渠氏，後入魏，以豪族徙北邊，仍家於五原郡。
units.literal: His grandfather Xin served the Juqu clan; later he entered Wei and, as a prominent clan, was relocated to the northern frontier, settling in Wuyuan Commandery.
units.idiomatic: His grandfather Xin served the Juqu clan; later he entered Wei and, as a prominent clan, was relocated to the northern frontier, settling in Wuyuan Commandery.

units.zh: 既至，會梁將嚴超達等軍逼涇州；
units.literal: When he arrived, the Liang generals Yan Chaoda and others were pressing Jing Province;
units.idiomatic: When he arrived, the Liang generals Yan Chaoda and others were pressing Jing Province;

units.zh: 又陳武帝率衆將攻廣陵，刺史王敬寶遣使告急；
units.literal: Chen Baxian was also leading a host of generals to attack Guangling; Governor Wang Jingbao sent envoys in urgent appeal;
units.idiomatic: Chen Baxian was also leading a host of generals to attack Guangling; governor Wang Jingbao sent envoys in urgent appeal;

units.zh: 復有尹思令率衆萬餘人，謀襲盱貽。
units.literal: Yin Siling too led more than ten thousand men, plotting a surprise attack on Xuyi.
units.idiomatic: Yin Siling too led more than ten thousand men, plotting a surprise attack on Xuyi.

units.zh: 韶謂諸將曰：「自梁氏喪亂，國無定主，人懷去就，強者從之。
units.literal: Shao said to the generals, "Since the Liang house fell into disorder, the state has had no fixed ruler; people weigh where to go and where to stay, following whichever side seems stronger.
units.idiomatic: Shao said to the generals, "Since the Liang house fell into disorder, the state has had no fixed ruler; people weigh where to go and where to stay, following whichever side seems stronger.

units.zh: 霸先等智小謀大，政令未一，外託同德，內有離心，諸君不足憂，吾揣之熟悉矣。」
units.literal: Baxian and the like have small minds and large ambitions; their orders are not unified — outwardly claiming unity, inwardly divided at heart. You need not worry, gentlemen; I know them thoroughly."
units.idiomatic: Chen Baxian and the like have small minds and large ambitions; their orders are not unified — outwardly claiming unity, inwardly divided at heart. You need not worry, gentlemen; I know them thoroughly."

units.zh: 乃留儀同敬顯儁、堯難宗等圍守宿預，自將步騎數千人倍道赴涇州。
units.literal: He left Equal-to-the-Three-Dukes Jing Xianjun, Yao Nazong, and others to besiege and hold Suyu; he himself led several thousand infantry and cavalry by forced march toward Jing Province.
units.idiomatic: He left Equal-to-the-Three-Dukes Jing Xianjun, Yao Nazong, and others to besiege and hold Suyu; he himself led several thousand infantry and cavalry by forced march toward Jing Province.

units.zh: 進與超達合戰，大破之，盡獲其舟艦器械。
units.literal: Advancing, he joined battle with Chaoda and routed them utterly, capturing all their boats and equipment.
units.idiomatic: Advancing, he joined battle with Chaoda and routed them utterly, capturing all their boats and equipment.

units.zh: 謂諸將士曰：「吳人輕躁，本無大謀，今破超達，霸先必走。」
units.literal: He told the officers and soldiers, "The Wu people are rash by nature and never had great plans. Now that Chaoda is broken, Baxian will surely flee."
units.idiomatic: He told the officers and soldiers, "The Wu people are rash by nature and never had great plans. Now that Chaoda is broken, Chen Baxian will surely flee."

units.zh: 即回赴廣陵。
units.literal: He at once turned back toward Guangling.
units.idiomatic: He at once turned back toward Guangling.

units.zh: 陳武帝果遁去。
units.literal: Chen Baxian indeed fled.
units.idiomatic: Chen Baxian indeed fled.

units.zh: 追至楊子柵，望揚州城乃還，大獲其軍資器物，旋師宿預。
units.literal: Pursuing as far as Yangzi stockade, he sighted Yangzhou city and turned back; he captured a great store of military supplies and equipment, then wheeled his army back to Suyu.
units.idiomatic: Pursuing as far as Yangzi stockade, he sighted Yangzhou city and turned back; he captured a great store of military supplies and equipment, then wheeled his army back to Suyu.

title.zh: 卷六十七 列傳第三十七 溫嶠 郗鑒
title.en: Volume 67 Biographies 37: Wen Jiao; Xi Jian
title.raw: 卷六十七 列傳第三十七 溫嶠 郗鑒 Volume 67 Biographies 37: Wen Jiao; Xi Jian

units.zh: 溫嶠
units.literal: Wen Jiao.
units.idiomatic: Wen Jiao.

units.zh: 溫嶠，字太真，司徒羨弟之子也。
units.literal: Wen Jiao, courtesy name Taizhen, was the son of Wen Dan, younger brother of Minister of Education Xian.
units.idiomatic: Wen Jiao, courtesy name Taizhen, was the son of Wen Dan, younger brother of Minister of Education Wen Xian.

units.zh: 父憺，河東太守。
units.literal: His father Dan was Administrator of Hedong.
units.idiomatic: His father, Wen Dan, served as administrator of Hedong commandery.

units.zh: 從兄旭，晞之別駕，恐禍及己，勸之赴召，鑒終不廻，晞亦不之逼也。
units.literal: His cousin Xu, Xi's aide, fearing disaster reaching himself, urged him to obey the summons; Jian never turned back; Xi also did not force him.
units.idiomatic: His cousin Xi Xu—Gou Xi's aide—feared for himself and urged compliance; Xi Jian still refused, yet Gou Xi did not press him.

units.zh: 及京師不守，寇難鋒起，鑒遂陷於陳午賊中。
units.literal: When the capital did not hold and bandit calamities sprang like spear-points, Jian thereupon fell among Chen Wu's bandit band.
units.idiomatic: When Luoyang fell and rebels multiplied, Xi Jian fell captive to Chen Wu's gang.

units.zh: 邑人張實先求交於鑒，鑒不許。
units.literal: Townsmen Zhang Shi earlier sought friendship with Jian; Jian refused.
units.idiomatic: A neighbor, Zhang Shi, had courted his friendship before; Xi Jian rejected him.

units.zh: 姚萇遣其子略攻湖城及上洛，又使其將楊佛嵩圍洛陽。
units.literal: Yao Chang sent son Lue attack Hucheng and Shangluo—also sent officer Yang Fosong besiege Luoyang.
units.idiomatic: Yao Chang struck Hucheng and besieged Luoyang.

units.zh: 恢遣建武將軍辛恭靖救洛陽，梁州刺史王正胤率眾出子午穀，以為聲援。
units.literal: Hui sent General Who Establishes Martial Xin Gongjing rescue Luoyang—Liangzhou Inspector Wang Zhengyin led hosts out Ziwu Valley as sounding support.
units.idiomatic: Xi Hui sent Xin Gongjing to Luoyang and Wang Zhengyin through Ziwu as diversion.

units.zh: 略懼而退。
units.literal: Lue feared and withdrew.
units.idiomatic: Yao Lue retreated.
